utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Witness 28. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. And, Mr. Re, are you ready to re-examine the witness? I think you indicated that you would need ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 28. I just want to ask you some questions to clarify some things that were asked of you in cross-examination yesterday. Do you have Exhibit MFI P21 -- 1212, which is the Human Rights Watch report, in front of you? It was in that bundle we gave you. That -- the folder. Has it been taken away from you? Yes, that one's fine. Yes. Okay. Yesterday, Mr. Harvey asked you a question. Can you please turn to page 92 of that particular document. I'll refer you to a question -- the Court to a question asked by Mr. Harvey at page 109 of the transcript and your answer --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It should be in there. There was also the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- hard binder which we gave you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have the page -- page 92 of that report. Yesterday at page 109 of the unpaginated transcript, you had said in response to a question from Mr. Harvey, "I think that middle July there was attempt of Serbian forces to suppress KLA existence in different villages. By then I think more than 40 per cent of territory was already controlled by KLA, as far as I can understand" -- there's a word I don't understand -- "the villages. So really what was happening, they would start pushing and bombarding the village by village." Now, if I could just take you to the Human Rights Watch report. And there's a passage at page 92 which says: "From April until mid July 1998, the UCK held as much as 40 per cent of the territory of Kosovo, although much of that territory was retaken by government forces by August 1998. Until then, however, the UCK had held a number of strategic towns and villages and manned check-points along some of Kosovo's important roads today" -- and this is written in October 1998 -- "their area of control has been reduced to some parts of Drenica and a few scattered pockets in the west, especially at night." Now, is what is written in that report which I've just quoted to you consistent with your observations and research in Kosovo in that period in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson cross-examined you yesterday about some portions of this report which is in front of you, and he asked you a number of questions. One of those at page 40 was whether information in the Human Rights Watch report -- not 40 of that; 40 of the transcript, page 20 -- referable to page 20 of that report and at page 12 of that report. And he asked you whether the information in the Human Rights Watch report accurately reflected information given to you by lawyers who you interviewed. And at page 41, whether it was consistent with information provided to you about detention during 1998. He was asking you to comment upon this report vis-a-vis your own experiences. Yesterday you gave some evidence about the conflict. And if I could take you to page 91 of the Human Rights Watch report, where it says: "The hostilities between the UCK and government forces had by February 28th, 1998 reached a level of conflict to which the obligations of Common Article 3 apply. Given the subsequent intensity of the conduct -- sorry, conflict from March through September, Human Rights Watch is also evaluating the conduct of the UCK and government forces based on the standards enshrined in protocol II to the Geneva Convention. On February 28th Serbian special forces launched their first large-scale military attack on villages Likosane and Cirez suspected of harbouring UCK members. Since that date the UCK and the government had been engaged in ongoing hostilities involving military offensives, front lines, and the use of attack helicopters and heavy artillery, mostly by the government. The UCK possesses small arms and light artillery. Although the UCK is primarily a guerilla army with no rigid hierarchical structure and there are separate internal factions during the period covered by this report, from September to -- from February to September, the UCK was organised -- was an organised military force for purposes of international humanitarian law." I'm not asking you for a -- an opinion as to the applicability of Common Article 3 or the application of international humanitarian law. What I'm going to ask you about is the conflict and what you observed. I want you to comment upon the accuracy of their assessment - that's the Human Rights Watch assessment - that there was a conflict in -- a conflict had commenced by the time of the attack on the 28th of February, 1998 based upon everything you saw as an observer on the ground and someone whose work was used by Human Rights Watch to form this assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that Mr. Re prefaces his question by indicating that he's not asking for an opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he actually is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if he wishes through this witness to establish factual material which may assist the Trial Chamber to reach that conclusion, then the right way to do it is to ask about the particular incidents that this witness is able to testify about, one by one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the whole issue of the existence of a armed conflict, of course, is directly linked to the applicability of Common Article 3, I would say, unless your concept of an armed conflict would be any different from what we find in the Geneva Conventions. Therefore, a few facts are given in this report. For example, light artillery in the hands of the UCK or other facts. But the way in which you phrased the question is the -- to comment on the accuracy of the Human Rights Watch assessment that in their assessment there was a conflict, that a conflict had commenced by the time, that is, as a matter of fact, another way of asking for a support or a denial of the conclusions of the Human Rights Watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Two -- two things in response. The Defence case, as I understand it, is there was no conflict --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- at that particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The second one is yesterday Mr. Emmerson asked the witness exactly the same in relation to other conclusions Human Rights Watch had drawn in relation to the conduct of -- or the behaviour of the Serbian police. My -- I'm asking this witness in effect: You were on the ground there. You saw what was happening. In --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there is a difference between asking about activities of the police and asking whether the conclusion that it was an armed conflict, which has such an important legal connotation, there is a difference. But you may ask about whether -- what this witness observed, whether that is consistent with what apparently, according to the report, Human Rights Watch used as facts underlying their conclusion; that is, that an armed conflict had emerged.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I simply add that in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- passage that Mr. Re read into the record, the second paragraph on page 91 contains factual information; that is to say, there was an attack on Likosane and Cirez on the 28th of February; there had been ongoing hostilities involving military offensives, front lines, and the use of attack helicopters and heavy artillery and that the UCK possessed small arms and light artillery. Apart from that, we would respectfully submit that none of that -- the material is properly the subject of a question seeking endorsement of the witness. Those -- those are matters of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's what I said before, I think. So you can ask the witness about the facts which Human Rights Watch reported as supporting their conclusion that there was an armed conflict. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness 28, Human Rights Watch used a number of incidents and facts which are referred to in the report to conclude that there was a conflict in existence by 28th of February, 1998. Did you observe any factual situations on the ground, conflicts, attacks, or anything like that, which are consistent with those used by Human Rights Watch to reach its -- to reach its opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reluctant now to comment on this part of Human Rights Watch report just for the pure fact that I -- on this part I didn't have any input given. I can just say that parallelly in the same period -- and I mentioned yesterday it was my opinion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have problems in receiving ... Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said, "I can just say that parallel in the same period. And I mentioned yesterday it was my opinion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My opinion was that there was a military conflict, and I mentioned why I did see that starting from 28th of February. I would remember a few more, I think, indications that could sustain that opinion, especially in Drenica. After that, police forces didn't enter deep into the region and I had a couple of interviews with the human rights workers and organisations that were going into the Drenica to supply the food to -- to the refugees. And they were stopped on the check-points by KLA. They were sometimes returned back, checked identity papers. So I -- I had feeling that there was established control there. Also, I visited Drenica several times and -- to talk about the situation with the refugees, because the villages in Drenica, bordering villages closer to Mitrovica, Srbica were shelled by Serbian forces. That was the reason I was going there. And I did see military command there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On what did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. To the extent that -- to the extent the witness has -- has answered factually, I have no objection to the extent she has rendered an opinion. We would interpose an objection with regard to there being the establishment of military conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith, you can't object to an answer of the witness. I mean, the question was now properly phrased. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, then I'll put it -- I'm put it another way then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can comment on it at a later stage that this was opinion rather than facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although, it was a mixed answer, and you expressed that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, to the extent -- to the extent that the Chamber directed that the answer be direct -- deal with facts in the answer -- and the answer obtained dealt with opinion, the objection is noted for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the Chamber directed the -- to ask for the facts. The Chamber never directs a witness to answer, unless there's a reason to do so. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting the Chamber did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It didn't escape our attention that a small part of the answer included the opinion of the witness as to the existence of an armed conflict. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just on that last answer, you said it was your opinion that there was military conflict, "And I mentioned why I did say that -- see that starting from the 28th of February." What were the -- the facts, circumstances, or things you observed which leads you to believe there was a military conflict from the 28th of February? What specific -- why that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that we addressed that question yesterday. The 28th of February there was that military operation against the Cirez and Likosane, which then was followed by the funeral with the presence of KLA soldiers. But the next event was, like, two or three days after, and it was Prekaz event with Adem Jashari family being sacrificed in that conflict. And dealing with the Jashari issue, I was aware that from January Jashari -- Jashari and the groups of KLA, I would say, at that point already have been hiding in the forests nearby and that Serbian police tried to arrest them. There was attack on Jashari family in the beginning of January, and then that -- that already was some kind of military unit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The final thing I want to ask you, Witness 28, is -- if you could just turn to page 92 of the Human Rights Watch report, where it says: "Seasoned war correspondents, such as Human Rights Watch researchers, who encountered the UCK, observed instances of discipline amongst UCK fighters manning check-points and their tendency to apply -- sorry, their tendency to apply similar policies and procedures, for example, with regard to granting journalists access to areas under UCK control. Such discipline is an indication that the fighters were receiving orders regarding policy that the fighters were answerable at least to regional commanders. There are also cases, however, when a clear lack of discipline was observed, which points to some structural weaknesses within the UCK. Despite this, it is clear the UCK leadership was able to organise systematic attacks throughout large parts of Kosovo." I just want to ask you the same -- the same sort of question. Did you encounter or experience anything similar to that which Human Rights Watch has used to make that finding in its report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do think they had their own pass to UCK zone, but the process was really that political representation in Pristina of KLA that existed at the time was issuing passes to the journalists and human rights workers that they can go and interview people on the territory. So I did have that pass. I believe that Fred Abrahams was also at that point a researcher for Human Rights Watch had that pass. I am -- only can remember one situation when that was broken in the sense of -- there were two journalists, but they were Serbian journalists, I think, or Russian, were kidnapped and kept for two days. And that's only what I remember, that journalists suffered. In -- in Drenica. I'm talking about Drenica region.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to follow up on that KLA pass. Are you telling the Trial Chamber that the KLA in Pristina gave you a pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell just the Trial Chamber who gave -- who gave you the pass, what it was valid for, how you used it, and how effective it was. And -- and when you got it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- this was not called "KLA." It was political representation of KLA. And Mr. Adem Demaci was then political representative of that office. And that office was approving the passes to -- into Drenica mostly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re put five questions in one to you. You answered the question who gave the pass to you. What was it valid for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was valid to enter the territory under the control of the KLA in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did it say that, "Valid to enter the territory under the control of the KLA," or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember what was written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then next question was: When was the pass issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was mid -- mid of the year that I got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mid of the year --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or second part -- second part of the year of 1988 [sic]. Before that, I was entering but I didn't need the pass. I knew the people. But I think second part of 1998 was this issued to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? Because "the second part" still covers six months.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six months. I think it must be early autumn or maybe something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Early autumn. Do I have to understand that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that. But would you call September early autumn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- then another part of the question was: How did you use it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never had to show that pass to anyone, because I knew the people who would just go with me there. So I just didn't need ever to prove who am I. But I understand that some foreign journalists had to -- encountered the KLA at check-points and show that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, earlier you said, "I didn't need the pass at an early stage because people knew me." But then you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then you apparently -- then you apparently -- the situation changed, and now you tell us that even when you had this pass, you still didn't use it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore any question about how effective it was, your personal --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My personal situation was slightly different than a journalist probably there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Re, no further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No further questions, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to check on a -- on a few matters with you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re took you to page 91 about the situation after the 28th of February. Human Rights Watch describes that "UCK and the government have been engaged in ongoing hostilities involving military offensive front lines." Did you ever see any front lines after February 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me think. I would not call that "front line." I would call that frozen -- from some periods during the year would be frozen military situation where KLA would keep part of the territory not disturbed by Serbian forces and then almost 100 metres, 200 metres further another check-point, and then there would be Serbian control of that. That was typical, I think, for Malisevo for a couple of months. And for -- for Orahovac I would say that was the front line at -- that lasted two or three days. But I was not there. I just could interview people who explained how situation happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And about the Dukagjini area, could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My -- my understanding was when I was in 29th -- and several days in this that there was a road dividing Decani, Djakovica. That was the road that was between -- between Serbian forces and KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said the 29th --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 29th and -- from 20th to 29th. I can just remember that, that after the fights that occurred on 22nd, 23rd, shelling from the -- the Suka Babaloc. I think the Serbian police succeeded to keep the road open and the villages were under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the month of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Month of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then did you -- any -- did you observe or learn about helicopters used for attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was told by Albanian refugees that military -- military planes, they call it, were used. But I was not sure is that for the attacks or for -- for -- to scare the people, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us about military planes --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that were reported to you. You understood that to be helicopters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Planes, I think. I think that they were saying "planes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you learn anything about the weaponry used -- Human Rights Watch says "heavy artillery mostly by the government."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heavy artillery, I think later, later in the conflict stage, especially in August and May. For heavy artillery, I'm not sure what was happening in April. I know that there was shelling. But how? What was the structure of the weaponry, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the UCK is described as possessing small arms and light artillery." Could you on the basis of your observation confirm that or ...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I cannot comment on weaponry that UCK had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Any need to re-examine the -- to ...? That's three times nodding "no." Since we have no further questions for you, Witness 28, this concludes your testimony before this Court; although we had a bit of a chaotic start last week, I hope that you also noticed that it was -- that we were better organised these days, although the Chamber still regrets that we could not already yesterday let you go. Thank you very much for coming back today. Thanking for -- I thank you for answering the questions of the parties and the questions put to you by the Bench, and I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now the curtains are down, so I think the witness can be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In respect of the next witness, Mr. Di Fazio is take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have problems in hearing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can hear you now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. The -- Mr. Di Fazio proposes to lead his evidence by Rule 92 ter, and I understand statements have been served, et cetera. Mr. Di Fazio will deal with that. Just in relation to what happens afterwards, that -- Mr. -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Haskaj, who doesn't want protective measures, is the only other witness we have available today, due to various matters concerning travel documents of witnesses coming from Kosovo hopefully tomorrow. Last night we filed an application to restore investigation team leader Harjit Sandhu to the witness list, he was originally on the list, but only for the limited purpose of his testifying about -- or providing evidence in written form we would make the application for in relation to the exhumation of the body of Mr. Skender Kuqi. As the Trial Chamber will appreciate, we made attempts to have relevant family members from the Kuqi family testify as to the exhumation of that particular body. It's one of the bodies which -- for which there was no DNA. It's one of the four bodies for which there was no DNA analysis undertaken. The body wasn't re-exhumed for DNA. And that evidence, in the absence of a family member, is needed to connect the body coming out of the cemetery with that which Dr. Morcillo performed an autopsy on. Now, Mr. Sandhu's evidence would be the fact that he attended on the 9th of March, 2004 a grave in -- in the cemetery and the family members pointed out the tended grave of their father and relative, Mr. Skender Kuqi, and Mr. Sandhu was present when the body was labeled and the label went with the body-bag and then Dr. Morcillo performed an autopsy on that particular body. That's the -- that's the evidence we would -- we would seek to elicit from Mr. Sandhu but in -- in written form. Now, we haven't got a 92 bis declaration yet. We could get that very quickly today or -- if we run out of witnesses today, I would seek to call him today for cross-examination, if necessary, if the Trial Chamber would allow us to restore him to the list for that very limited purpose. He's in the building and he's available at five minutes' notice to -- to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen the -- you said it was filed yesterday late. I was informed about that you intended to file it. My latest information early this morning, because I have to check my e-mails late at night, early in the morning, was that it had not yet been filed but that you intended to file it and that a courtesy copy was provided to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We electronically filed it last night but it wouldn't have been distributed by the Registry until this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I haven't read it although I was informed about it, but let's first ask the Defence about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm in the same position that Your Honour is in. Apparently, it was received by way of e-mail sometime very late last night. It may be - I don't know - in due course if it's a matter capable of relatively easy resolution, but it doesn't, if I may say so, sound like it would take up very much time in court today whatever way the matter is resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so may I suggest that rather than try to, so to speak, deal with this at break-neck speed, that we have the opportunity to consider it, discuss it with the Prosecution, and resolve it over the coming days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that Mr. Re would like to use the time remaining today, which, of course, would ask for a quick resolution of -- of the motion filed and a quick response. Could we -- could we invite perhaps the parties during the first break to -- to see what could be achieved and then we'll read the motion meanwhile as well and then we'll see after the break whether there's a problem which the Chamber would have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- determine matters or whether the parties could agree on, a very practical matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This may -- this may be of some assistance. I was able to give the 92 ter statement of the next witness to my client this morning, because I only received it late last night in the language that he speaks. And I was -- I've already indicated that I may -- I may need some time to take instructions with regard to the new 92 ter statement, because there are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I did --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- there are some changes also with regard to the motion filed. I'm aware of its existence, but I have not had an opportunity to take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, of course, I did not find the time to compare in detail the earlier statements taken by the next witness and the 92 ter statement. I just couldn't find time for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There -- there's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I received it only a couple of minutes before court. Are the differences such that the 92 ter statement introduces new elements which could not already have been considered on the basis of the statements which one would expect to be used for --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- preparation of cross-examination rather than some --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are some deviations. I don't think it's going to take a particularly long time in the event that I need to take instructions with regard to it at all. I'm offering it as an understanding of the fact that we may need a bit longer of a break, so we may be able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- as we would say, grab two birds out of the bush, instead of only one, with regard to scheduling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop and Mr. Emmerson, as far as the 92 ter statement is concerned, I -- I can imagine that Mr. Guy-Smith is -- is even more interested than you are in this 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We would obviously be grateful for the opportunity to have a brief consultation in connection with the changes, but, of course, we've taken instructions on the basis of the original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's not going to take us very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest that we start already with the witness to see whether the witness recognises signatures, et cetera, et cetera, so we start with the 92 ter procedure, have a break a little bit earlier than usual, a little bit longer than usual, and then after the break we'll hear whether we can continue with the cross-examination. And if the Defence considers that that's not possible, the Chamber will make a ruling whether or not we'll start.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that's -- I think that's probably going to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And is an excellent suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. If Your Honours please, could we deal with it in this way: As you say, go through the formal procedures and get him to recognise his statement. But I would then, if it's okay with the Trial Chamber, perhaps if we could take the break there. I was hoping to avow myself of the break to just clear up one or two matters that I need to do before I finish my examination-in-chief. And it will be brief. It will be brief. I'm thinking in the order of 10, 15 minutes of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then finish your examination-in-chief after the break? MR. DI FAZIO: That's what I'm thinking. Unless you would, of course, prefer to deal with it all at once after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the Chamber, also for logistical purposes, would like you to finish examination-in-chief before the break. So if there are any questions left, apart from that, the Defence now asks for additional time to consider whether they could accept the 92 ter statement, but we take it that the Prosecution should have been ready to call this witness and -- even without these delays. Let's just assume that the Defence had said, No, it's all fine with us. Let's continue. Then you would have been in the same position. MR. DI FAZIO: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore the Chamber would like you to -- yes, to conclude your examination-in-chief before the break. Then I think the witness can be brought into the courtroom. I see the Chamber staff has allowed us to -- allows us now to have a good comparative view on the earlier statement and the present statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it was not Chamber staff but, rather, the Prosecution who provided the version which is -- has that been made available to the Defence as well? So you have a comparative -- okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Haskaj. Can you understand -- can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haskaj. Please be seated. Madam Usher, could you assist the witness in getting his earphones in such a way that they don't fall off all the time. Witness, if you -- yes. Please be seated, Mr. Haskaj. Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Examination by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Haskaj. Could you just tell the Trial Chamber, please, if these details are -- are correct. You're born on the 25th of March, 1978 and your place of birth was Irzniq in Decan municipality. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a copy of a statement. You'll see it appearing on the screen in front of you. Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 2142, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as P1213.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I wonder if we could -- it's the Albanian version that we need to look at in this particular regard. Could we scroll down to the bottom of that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Haskaj, did -- is that a statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we just have a look at the remaining pages, please. Move through them and look at the bottom of each page so that you can identify signatures. And just tell us if your signature appears at the bottom of the remaining pages.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps we don't need to go through the entire statement doing that. Was that a statement that you reviewed and made some changes to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: [No verbal response] MR. DI FAZIO: I didn't get an answer to that, not one that I heard anyway.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Do I have to read it all to be able to see whether it's the same one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I don't think it's necessary. You -- yesterday did you review the statement that you had produced and given to OTP investigators earlier on the 5th of -- on the 18th of February, 2006, and did you yesterday review that statement that you gave in February 2006 and make some small changes to it -- to it that you wished to?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And is the statement that you see in front of you in an electronic form that statement which you reviewed and later signed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if you were to be asked questions about the material that is contained in that statement, would you provide answers that are consistent with the material that is in that statement? In other words, would you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, of course, there's -- I can imagine there's some confusion. I take it that the witness went through his February 2006 statement. That's the statement he reviewed. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then made some changes to that. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the new statement was -- MR. DI FAZIO: The new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- produced. Of course, to that statement he didn't make -- he didn't review that again and -- but did he read it then again? Have you read the final version in your own language? Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's what you signed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And are the contents true and accurate to the best of your belief and knowledge?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, you refer to a few annexes. And I just want to very briefly take you to some of them -- or take you to all of them, but I shan't dwell on them at length. Firstly, the -- the first annex. It's -- or rather, group of annexes. It's 65 ter 2139, and it consists of three sketches. Could we look at that, and in particular could we look at the first sketch, also known as annex 1. I believe that there are English translations in e-court as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, do they need separate exhibit numbers? Or are they part of the statement? I have not checked earlier. MR. DI FAZIO: They are referred to and are part of the statement. Could Your Honours just bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, if we would scroll down in the statement, we would find them attached. So therefore -- is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: No, they're separate documents, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Separate documents. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, separate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then they need numbers. Could you -- is it a set of several -- I remember -- MR. DI FAZIO: There's essentially - one, two, three - three items. First is a bundle or -- or group of three sketches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I take it that you want to have these three sketches -- MR. DI FAZIO: They can be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... At a later stage. Then do they have one or several -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I'd be happy with one exhibit number for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But just for the registrar to know, are they known under different 65 ter numbers or under one 65 ter number? So that he knows what ... MR. DI FAZIO: One 65 ter number. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For three sketches. MR. DI FAZIO: For three sketches. It's 2139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1214, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to look at -- in particular, look at the sketch number 2. And you'll see it's got a number "2" on the top left-hand corner. Okay. And perhaps for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and Defence counsel, could we also have a brief look at the English translation of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and have it rotated so that we can read what it says. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I'm only interested in one aspect of it. Having seen it and I'd just like to invite the Trial Chamber to look at that note -- the word "kitchen" down -- that's what I'm going to be asking about. The word "kitchen" on the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. Perhaps we can now go back to the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, that's a sketch you produced. And in there you referred to "Ruzhina" or "Ruzhina," kitchen. Now, how far away was that particular place from the Black Eagles base, the place where you slept and ate?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. I can give you it in roundabout manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just do the best. Give us an approximation.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: One kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is that place, the kitchen, the -- where is that in -- in relation to the headquarters of the Dukagjini Operational Zone, or is it the same place?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you just describe what was at the Dukagjini headquarters -- or the Dukagjini Operational Zone to the Trial Chamber. What exactly was there in that complex?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: It was a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we know there was a kitchen there as well. Anything else? House, kitchen. Or was that it?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: It was a house that also had a kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear enough. Did you ever have reason to go there when you were a member of the Black Eagles?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, we did go there to take our meals.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, just for my orientation. Mr. Haskaj, on the sketch we found -- we find, in the middle of it, a kind of a fork where one road goes a bit up and the other one goes a bit down. Is that fork, is that the centre of Glodjane village where to the left it goes to Irzniq, to the right it goes to Saptej, and to the south, so down, it goes in the direction of Gramocelj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to the bifurcation that goes upwards or the one that goes downwards?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one most in the centre of the -- of your sketch; that is, where it goes down in the direction of the kitchen and where going up it says "700 metres."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the centre of the village of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you also tell us approximately from this fork to the kitchen what approximately was the distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About three to four hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So would that still be in the village, not yet in the outskirts of where the -- where there still are houses in the village? Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement that you -- we've been -- I referred you to earlier, you say that you -- you recall seeing Mr. Haradinaj in the canteen where the Black Eagles unit used to eat. Is --

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. The kitchen that you've marked there, that's the unit where the Black Eagles used to eat; correct? Canteen, rather.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how often in the time that you were a member of the Black Eagles and based in Glodjane would you go there to eat? Was it every night or was it in -- less frequently? Can you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: In the beginning, it was every night. But later when the fighting started and became more frequent, it was made impossible for us to go there every day or every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Certainly. And when you went there with your fellow Black Eagles members, was Mr. Balaj with you?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, there were occasions when he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to look at a map now, if I may. And that, if Your Honours please, is referred to as 61 ter 2140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would need, Mr. Registrar? MR. DI FAZIO: 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would need a number, and it would be, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1215, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While and -- just before I ask you about this map, one other matter that perhaps needs a little clarification. Earlier in your -- in your evidence, you were describing the headquarters of the Dukagjini Operational Zone, and I asked you about what was there and you said, "It was a house." And you talked about the kitchen being there as well. Whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in addition to it being used as an eating place and a headquarters, whether families or civilians resided there or whether it was given over entirely to military use?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: No, there was no one from any family there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thanks. All right. Look at the map that is in front of you. Is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, has an attempt been made to ask the witness to identify it from an aerial view whether he recognises? Because we have in evidence some aerial views of the village of Glodjane, so -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, yes, we could do that now, if you prefer, rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I am -- I've forgotten about the exact numbers. I think it's P35 or something like that. It's -- MR. DI FAZIO: We've got a map that we -- is now part of his statement that is an aerial view in itself, and I intend to produce that to -- to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm willing to show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- several. We have one ... Yes, and -- we have two different kinds of aerial views. The one is the one you have there, and the other one would be, Mr. Registrar? That would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's marked for identification as P35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P35. Yes, well, my memory is still serving me to some extent well. P35 could be considered as well, which is more or less a -- as -- as if it were a map. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you would perhaps -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yep. I'll -- I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- find out which one would serve this purpose best. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness, could you have a look at the screen in front of you. And you -- it's an aerial map, almost like a satellite map. Looking at that little village there from this angle, can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Not from this angle, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you use the other picture, then perhaps that would work better and then we could -- if that doesn't work, then we could give it a try again with this and perhaps give some guidance to the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Thank you. Well, in that case, we can go directly to the photo, then. Perhaps we can look at 65 ter 2141. I have a large version which -- I don't know if you -- it would be better on the ELMO or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it's on our screen, then it's -- MR. DI FAZIO: I don't know if it makes much difference really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The advantage of having it on the screen is that you can point at certain matters. Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. That's as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I take it -- this is a marked version, so, of course, it could be that it's just a 65 ter number, but it looks very much as if this is a document already marked and perhaps in -- oh, it's marked by this witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, Witness, are those your initials that you placed on that map -- sorry, that photograph yesterday?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And does -- does the -- the circled area with your initials Y.H. just underneath that, is that the school that -- the elementary school that the Black Eagles had their base?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's where they slept for a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then also ask the witness whether the canteen is visible on this picture. I don't think it ... MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether -- where you said the canteen was, whether that's -- that can be seen on this picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see it from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, if you -- or if we could have the pointer at the -- no, I mean not the pointer but the -- the cursor on this picture. And could you please move further to the right down. Yes, a little bit further down to where a fork is in the roads. Yes, a little bit more to the left. Yes. Would that be the fork I earlier asked you about, the road to the left --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could you tell us, is it then the canteen in which direction? Is that to the right down that road? Madam Usher, perhaps you could try to move the cursor in -- a little bit -- yes. Is that down that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further down that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a bit further down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A little bit further down. Okay. Could we then move again to the map, Mr. Di Fazio, that -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which was P35. MR. DI FAZIO: P35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could that be on the screen. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now could you -- yes. Madam Usher, could you please point with the cursor at the fork in the middle on the top of the photograph. Mr. Haskaj -- And if the parties would disagree with the guidance I give to Mr. Haskaj, then I take it that they'll immediately respond. Where the cursor is now on your screen, as far as we can be aware, that's the same fork we talked about earlier, direction of Irzniq going up to the top of the map; direction of Saptej going to the right; and direction of Gramocelj, which I understood was the road in the direction of the kitchen, going to the left further down. That's -- you see the cursor moving there. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're able to identify where the canteen was, Madam Usher will slowly move the cursor on this picture. Could you say "stop" if we are at the point where you think the canteen would have been.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have been able to help you on a -- on a larger map. It's very difficult for me to do it with any exactness. I can only point to the whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can -- we can zoom in a bit. Is this the maximum zooming in? Are you now able to better ... Yes, could we do the same exercise. Madam Usher, we are now at the fork and she's slowly moving.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where -- if you can identify the place approximately where the kitchen is, please tell us to stop. Could you slowly move, Madam Usher. So we're now coming close to where a little road goes to the right and to the front. We move on in the direction of Gramocelj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It -- it must be somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Could this be marked by the witness. Could you just mark that, add a "K" for "kitchen."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P1216.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I interrupted you very much, Mr. Di Fazio, but -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful to Your Honour for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we return now to ... MR. DI FAZIO: We can go back -- if we've finished with this, I think we can just go back to the photo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll go back to the photo, because that needs a number -- or has it been assigned a number already? Let me just check. The photograph has not been assigned a number yet, Mr. Registrar, has it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that, will be marked for identification as P1217.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the -- the picture marked by the witness before he came to court which indicates where the Black Eagles -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- headquarters were. MR. DI FAZIO: There's just one other feature I need to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. MR. DI FAZIO: So if we could get it up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's one other marking. That's an arrow. Does that show the direction of the Ekonomija farm?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately. It's in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have -- ever have reason to go there with your colleagues from the -- the Black Eagles?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Could you ask the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you and Black Eagles members ever go to the Ekonomija farm or the area at the Ekonomija farm, that -- the land around it, for any particular reason, any reason at all, in the time that you were based in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: It is possible that we went, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- okay. Well, fine. Fair enough. But if you did go, what sort of reasons would have taken you there? Training or some other reason?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I said that I can't remember that I've been there. There was no reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, you say that you did your training at the elementary school, which we can see circled there. Is that the only place that you trained?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And it's been given a number, but I would ask that it be fully exhibited, this photograph, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it would be -- yes, the photograph is not attached directly to the statement, is it? MR. DI FAZIO: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against the admission of the marked photograph outside of court? Then it is admitted into evidence, it being number ... Let me just check. P1217. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Right. If we could just return now, please, to 65 ter 2141. That's the photo -- the map rather. Sorry, 2140. My apologies. 2140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that ...? Has a number already been assigned to the map? Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, it's P1215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness, is -- is your signature or initials, do they appear on that -- on that map? Perhaps if we can make it smaller so that we can see it in perspective.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that a map that you marked when you originally provided your February 2006 statement?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And in your -- in that statement that you -- which you reviewed yesterday and later made some alterations, do you refer -- sorry. In -- yesterday you reviewed your 2006 statement and produced and signed another statement with some variations in it. In your new statement which I showed you this morning, do you refer to that particular map and comment on the various markings on it?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Both in the statement and about the map, I was asked which villages were better organised during the period May to end of July. And I remember that I marked some of the villages that were better organised during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Then the map is admitted into evidence. And that's P1215. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Your Honours, I think I've just about finished. We have numbers now for the bundle of sketches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to deal with -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a number of sketches since they are -- or we could deal with them, perhaps, already even if we have not yet dealt with the 92 ter statement, because even apart from the 92 ter statement these sketches are -- have some relevance on the basis of the viva voce testimony given by the witness. Any objections against the three sketches? Not. Then they are admitted into evidence. And that was number -- I think it was P1214, if I'm not wrong. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, admitted into evidence, all three of them, English translations attached. If you have no further questions, Mr. Di Fazio, we'll first have a break. Could I just enquire with the Defence: It's now 23 minutes past 10.00. If we would resume at 5 minutes to 11.00, would that be sufficient time? A little bit --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break and we'll resume at 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine the witness? But perhaps before we start, is there any update for the Chamber on matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's progress being made, is the short answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps it would be wisest, if progress has been made, not at this moment to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. Progress is being, rather than has been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think in many languages, you have expressions of chickens breeding eggs. I leave that for the -- not to compare you with these birds, but ... Then before I give you an opportunity to start to cross-examine the witness, then ... Mr. Haskaj, we were informed that you prepared a kind of a statement in writing in your own language. I've seen it. I've not seen any translation of that. So I do not know what it contains. It is unusual for a witness to deliver speeches. If at the end of your testimony there is any answer which you say I'd like to add something to this answer or I might have been misunderstood there, you have an opportunity to do so. But a witness, apart from that, should limit himself to what he's asked by the parties. Now, the statement you have put on paper and which we have not received any translation from has been provided to the parties. So if there's anything relevant in your statement for this case, then the parties will elicit that from you by questioning you on that matter. If, however, the statement was more of a general character, then it would be inappropriate for you as a witness to give such a statement. So you have to rely on the parties. They will consider how relevant or irrelevant it is what you did put on paper. And if they ask you questions, of course you can answer those questions. If they do not ask you any questions about it, then we leave your statement as it is; that is, on paper with you. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed. I think Defence counsel have received the statement not with a translation but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, we've received the document that Your Honour is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And have had an opportunity to obtain, so far as counsel are concerned, a gist -- a gist translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it entirely in your hands. This kind of statement sometimes tend to contain general observations on matters which are not for a witness to -- to comment upon. I leave it in the hands of the parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Haskaj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Haskaj -- Mr. Emmerson is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj, and he'll now cross-examine you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Haskaj, I'd like you, please, to look at paragraph 34 of your witness statement, which is Exhibit P1213, on page 7. It will be brought up on the screen in front of you in just a moment. Now, this document has been amended following your meeting yesterday with the Prosecutor, and I'm going to suggest to you that much of the information in that paragraph, at least in the way it's expressed, is wrong or inaccurate. And in particular, there is the suggestion in the second sentence and the third sentence that large portions of the Dukagjin area, including the Lake Radoniq area, were outside Serbian control between April and September and indeed that a number of villages, Gllogjan, Ratishe, Jabllanice, Dashinoc, Smolica, and Junik could not be entered by the Serb forces between April and September, and finally the suggestion that throughout that period, apparently, the greater part of the canal area that you marked on the map was controlled, as the word appears in your statement, by the KLA. That's the broad suggestion that I'm going to put to you. Now let me break it down, please. First of all, we have heard unchallenged evidence in this case, indeed from senior Serb military officials, that the 52nd Military Police Battalion was stationed in the area of the village of Bites and the base of Suka Bites from March onwards throughout the year. Can you comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: In a map I was shown yesterday I surrounded -- I marked the lake part, which was always under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And there were Serb forces based at the base of Suka Bites. You accept that.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were conducting operations and shelling from that position all the way over to Gllogjan and Irzniq throughout the period from the end of March, beginning of April through to September, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were Serb forces stationed in Junik throughout the indictment period from the PJP, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because on the face of your statement, you have suggested -- I mean, I don't know whether these are your words or somebody else's -- that between April and September Serb forces could not enter Junik. But that's not right, is it? They were based there and they did enter there.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I did not say that they did not enter. I mentioned only the villages where the KLA was better organised, and those were the villages that I mentioned. But I didn't say that they could not enter. I said yesterday several times that we did not have the armament, the weapons to keep everything under control, so we could never say that we had full control over a zone. In order for us to have had full control, we must have had a better organisation than that. This is what I said yesterday, and we discussed this a long time, and still they left it as it was, almost as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's quite important, this, because whether they're your words or somebody else's, you've signed the statement and you've said in the evidence that you've already given that its contents are accurate. But if you just take, for example, Junik, which you have said in that statement could not be entered by the Serb forces. I mean, that's just completely wrong, isn't it? It was not only entered by the Serb forces, but they were stationed in Junik at various points in time during the indictment period of March to September.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you say as well in this statement, as it appears, that Serb forces couldn't enter Gllogjan between April and the major offensive in September. But -- but we know from other evidence that there was a major offensive right through that area between the 9th and the 11th of August. You were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you take part in that offensive at all? Were you involved in the fighting between the 9th and 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So -- so, again, help us, how does it come about in your statement that it suggests that -- that the villages you've listed -- and I'll just read you the words as they appear in English. Having listed the villages including Gllogjan, you first of all say: "Between April and September the KLA was stronger in these villages than in other villages." We understand that. But then you go on in the statement to say: "The Serbian forces could not enter these villages during this period of time." I mean, that -- that's just not right, is it?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: That's not correct. But in the statement I prepared yesterday, when we made the amendments -- I was tired yesterday, as a matter of fact. I couldn't look at everything point by point and study it properly, because I arrived here at 2.00 and we continued working until 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did anybody mention to you that -- that the Trial Chamber has video footage of the Serbian offensive and a map from a senior Serbian official drawing the offensive of Serbian police and military running right through Gllogjan and Irzniq between the 9th and the 11th of August? Did anybody on the Prosecution team point that out to you at all?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where it says in your statement "the Serbian forces could not enter these villages during that -- this time," whose words are those? Were they words you spoke or words that somebody else suggested to you and you agreed with?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yesterday I mentioned it several times that this has to be changed, and I meant exactly this sentence. And they said, "It's not important." Well, I said, "This is not my words. Even if it's not important, it has to be changed."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it goes on in the new text to say that: "The area of the canal leading to Radoniq Lake was controlled" -- I emphasize that word, "controlled," -- "by the KLA except for the beginning of the blue highlight near Lluka and Isniq, which was controlled by the Serbs." Now, again, we have heard evidence in this case including evidence from a Serb official that there were armed engagements in the area of the canal from the 1st of July or the beginning of July onwards between the KLA and Serb forces. And the suggestion I'm putting to you is that -- that there was in effect a disputed area of territory around there with skirmishes taking place.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, again, were those your words as they appear in the statement, or were they words that were suggested to you and that you agreed with?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: The lawyers insisted on a different thing. And when I saw the statement, I said that many points have to be changed, because a different meaning comes out of this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: So some words had to be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can we turn to the question of the deployments that you've described. Could we look, please, at the photograph you marked, Exhibit P1217. Now, I just want to orientate ourselves a little, first of all. You say in your statement that you -- I want to make sure I've got this absolutely accurate. Bear with me a second. That -- that to your recollection, the Black Eagles was formed on the 14th of May; that you joined soon after. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in paragraph 13 of your statement, you say: "Our base was eventually set up in an elementary school in Gllogjan." And I want to ask you about the word "eventually." How long after you joined was it that you began to be based in that school? Let's take you personally, first of all.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly, but not a long time elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just help us if you can, please. Could it have been several weeks between you joining and you basing yourself in the school?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say in your statement that you left the Black Eagles at the end of July and that prior to you leaving, you had for some time been assigned to the villages of Voksh, Sllup, and Drenoc because of Serb attacks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we're -- we're focusing on a period between May and July. Can you remember so far as your period in Voksh, Sllup, and Drenoc was concerned, was that during June?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. It could have been June, about somewhere halfway through the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was it for several weeks?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So -- so just in terms of identifying how much time you personally were spending or had spent at the building that you've marked staying there, can you help us? Are we speaking about sometime between the end of May and some period in June? Is that to be understood correctly or not?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in terms of -- of who was there in that building, can I suggest to you that there were quite a number of KLA volunteers from all sorts of different types of groups and units at that school.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It wasn't specifically a Black Eagles base.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I said it earlier as well. That was not a base as such, but it was a place where we spent the night for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As did quite a number of other volunteers and groups of KLA volunteers.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. There were a lot of others.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you remember a man called Bedri Shala?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was not involved with the Black Eagles, was he?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he was conducting training there of KLA volunteers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Emmerson, you misrepresented the 92 ter statement where you said that the witness joined the Black Eagles soon after they were established. I think the 92 ter statement tells us that on the first day it was established - that's the 14th of May - that he joined it. I don't think it was of vital importance there, but paragraph 10 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, I was looking at the beginning of paragraph 11. It may be that I -- sorry. I was looking at the beginning of paragraph 11. It may be that I misread it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was in the beginning of paragraph 10. "I joined the Black Eagles on the first day that it was formed."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we don't need a lengthy discussion about it, but just so that we have everything clear on the record. Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Haskaj, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who is counsel for Mr. Balaj. Please proceed. Mr. Guy-Smith, thinking back to yesterday, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- question very focused. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday I was quite detailed. I thought that was the criticism.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Haskaj, you spent a relatively short period of time in training before you went to battle in Voksh; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It was, in fact, a matter of days before the pressures of the attacks were such that you and members of the Black Eagles, including Mr. Balaj, went to Voksh to perform your duties as a special intervention unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you got to Voksh, you remained in that area - by that I mean Voksh, Drenoc, and Sllup, those particular villages - because that is where the fights were occurring and where you were needed in order to battle; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
