utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You didn't come back to the area of Irzniq until sometime in July, after you were wounded; true?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I went there only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your statement, you indicate that -- in your statement, you indicate that you had a sniper rifle - that's in paragraph 20 -- I'm sorry, it's in paragraph 19. Were you given special training or were you one of the special soldiers who had engaged in that particular art, the art of sniping, so that you had a -- a keen eye and were used for a very specific purpose within the special unit?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did use it for shooting. And that's all the training that I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were fighting in -- in Voksh, Drenoc, and Sllup in June throughout July, except for the one time that you said you returned on one occasion, your commander, Idriz Balaj, was there also fighting with you, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, when following the testimony, I have difficulties in orienting myself where Voksh is exactly. But I may have missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, shall we go to a map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if -- if you say it's there and there, then I'll find it on the map, if it's at least on one of the maps which is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, it's definitely on a map in evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the witness can probably confirm those areas on the west side of the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The west side of the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you stopped fighting with the Black Eagles, you then returned to working with the village guard, or were you working with the KLA when you were back in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were you then under the command of Shemsedin Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he returned to that village a little earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The Black Eagles were still -- after your return, the Black Eagles were still out in the field, to your knowledge, were they not, engaged in fighting in various battles that were occurring throughout the region; true?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, as a unit, the Black Eagles were moving in and out of the area after you returned in July wherever their abilities and services were needed, depending on the battles that were occurring from July until certainly the September offensive; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us as you sit here today, if you remember, how much of the time that you saw the Black Eagles, and specifically Idriz Balaj, in Irzniq sitting around, shall I say, drinking coffee, as opposed to away from Irzniq fighting? Do you remember how much you saw him during that period of time after you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: There wasn't a single moment to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you indicated in your statement or you said in your statement that there -- there was no deputy commander or sub-commander, that -- that Idriz Balaj was known, who was also known as the commander or Toger, was the one who ran the unit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was -- and I'm using kind of a term of art here. He was the first in battle and the last out of battle. He was a man who -- who stayed with his soldiers and did not shirk from the responsibility of fighting, did he?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, once again in your statement you've indicated that once a shot was fired in the region that could be heard, he would immediately, when you were not in a particular battle, he would immediately move the special unit or -- or parts of the special unit to wherever those shots were coming from in order to operate as a special intervention unit to deal with the fact of the Serbian attacks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you living in Kosovo in 2002?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 30, you discuss an assassination attempt on Mr. Balaj's life in which his wife lost her leg and he had a fair amount of shrapnel in his body as a result of a bomb at his home. Correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that during that assassination attempt his wife also was with child, which she lost?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, that event was an event that was publicised in the television and in newspapers, was it not? The assassination attempt on -- on Idriz Balaj's life.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you saw pictures of the damaged home, as well as photographs, of both Idriz Balaj and his wife on television as well as in newspaper articles at the time it occurred, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After the assassination attempt, Mr. Balaj, which you've also indicated, was arrested and put on trial, and the trial was called the Dukagjin trial; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: By that time, you had been working with him for some time in the TMK, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When he was arrested and put on trial in the Dukagjin trial, once again that was a widely publicised matter throughout the country of Kosovo, was it not?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, again, likenesses of his -- or photographs of him were put on television as well as photographs of him were seen in newspapers, by you; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, during that period of time Idriz Balaj was identified as being "Toger" publicly throughout the country, was he not?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to turn, if I could, for a moment to P1214. If we could have that up on the screen, please. I'd -- I suppose we have -- well, let's do it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like for, if you could, please, if you could identify a couple of the other areas that are drawn on this map. And, first of all, taking a look at what's identified as Shtepija Ime, that was your house; correct? And that's on the left-hand side of the --

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- of the document where you've written those words, where there's a box; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And next to that was the headquarters of the KLA where Shemsedin Cekaj was headquartered; true?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you've indicated -- you've indicated on the map "Stabi UCK" to indicate where the headquarters were. Right?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, turning to the other part of the diagram. There's a place that says "Shkolla," and that school is a school which is up on top of a hill, which is a high school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that is an area which during the time was one of the places where on occasion the Black Eagles would go for training; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the area up there there's a school and there's a huge field, a huge flat area in front of the school, which would be available for callisthenics or war training; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Going down from -- going down from where it says "Shkolla," there is another place where you have drawn a -- an area which I understand is -- is that what you were saying is the small house where the Black Eagles were ultimately stationed in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they stayed there for a few days. I can't recall exactly. However, after the unit returned from the Voksh area, they stayed there for a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Directly across from -- from that area, which I take it is -- is a road, there is nothing. And as a matter of fact, there is a wide open field there which is another area which was available for military training and manoeuvres; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That -- that was an area that was used by both the Black Eagles on occasion as well as by the local KLA who were in the village of Irzniq; true?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. That's where military training took place, including other soldiers as well as the Black Eagles on occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, between the place on that map where you have the word "Gllogjan" and you have the word "Deqan," in that area was a mosque; true? And perhaps with the assistance --

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: The mosque is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With the -- perhaps with the assistance of the usher, we could have him mark this and I will get a new identification number.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: This is where the mosque is. And over there is a surgery, a doctor's surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You -- you've drawn two circles, one in which you've put an "A," which I -- I take it stands for the beginning of "ambulance"; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That's where the surgery is. And the mosque, further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the month of August 1998, you were in Irzniq; correct?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that period of time -- and you were just speaking a moment ago with Mr. Emmerson concerning an offensive that occurred in early August. During that period of time - and by that I'm referring to the first two weeks, for example, in August - you did not see Idriz Balaj in that area - and by that I mean -- by that I mean in Irzniq - on a constant basis, did you?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I can't remember seeing him there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember how often you saw him or if you saw him at all during the month of August in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I can't remember ever having seen him after my return from Voksh.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There came a time when the manpower of the Black Eagles was seriously -- seriously depleted. I'm wondering whether you know anything at all about that. You may, you may not, because you were no longer a Black Eagle. But there came a time when the number of men who were fighting in the Black Eagles, which went from the number which you've mentioned apart from the casualties that occurred, went down to about four or five men. Do you know about that? And if you do, fine; if you don't, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: As far as I know, the numbers were reduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And by the time of the September offensive, the -- the numbers of Black Eagles were about five. Do you know about that? And those were Naim Dashi, Jusuf Osmoni, Nagip Qelaj, and Agim Ramosaj, and, of course, Idriz Balaj. Those were -- those were the men left standing.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I do not know this exactly name by name, but I know that the numbers were very small. It was a very small number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, before we continue, the -- you've done with the sketch which was marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it needs a number. And it ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked for identification as D204.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you want to tender that, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- then D204 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: No re-examination, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Haskaj, you said that you had to go to Voksh. Do you remember exactly when that was?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, but it must have been during the first half of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Until the end of July, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, you said you were wounded, you returned, and I think your mother looked after you. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: First of all, I had to go to hospital to have the wound cleaned and to receive treatment, after which time I returned home and my family looked after me, that is, my mother and my sisters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your -- that was the family home in the centre of the village of ...?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, quite a lot of questions were put to you about whether you saw Mr. Balaj in that area. You said, "I don't remember that I saw him in August." What was your daily life in the month of August? Were you staying in the village? Were you ...?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: After I recovered, almost every day I took part in fighting in villages such as Prejlep, Carrabreg, and some other villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So much of the time you were not in Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Well, during the fighting for two or three or four hours I took part in that fighting. Then I went back, rested, and then returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You returned every day to Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So even when you were participating in the fighting in early August, as you told Mr. Emmerson, you would return every night home?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were you during this period of time in the month of August, were you aware about where exactly the unit you belonged to before - that's the Black Eagles - where they were participating in any combat activity? I mean, would you meet them? Would you see them when you were on the battleground in -- in Prilep? Or did you know anything about where they were engaged in combat activity?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not know where they were. They were participating in fighting, but as to where, I don't know. They were wherever the Serb forces were attacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then they should have been at many places at the same time, isn't it? Or was that just Serb forces attacking at one place?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: In the places where the attacks were the strongest and where there was more need for the Black Eagles to support, to offer support, or where there were families that needed protection and they had to fight against the Serbs so that the population had a chance to withdraw or go somewhere else. But I couldn't tell you where exactly, what village, they fought, because I was not with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you, apart from, as you tell us now, being aware that they were engaged in combat, did you ever see any part of this unit or the whole of the unit during these times?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I saw members of the unit, but not the whole unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where did you see them? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I remember seeing one of my co-villagers -- or some of my co-villagers, because some of them were members of the unit. And when they came to rest, it happened that I saw some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us anything about the frequency with which you saw them resting in the place where you lived or the place where you were.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: Well, during that period, I probably saw them two or three times. One or two of the soldiers that were members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 25 of your statement - and I'll just read that to you: "The second (or new) Black Eagles headquarters was set up only 400 metres from my house. It was a single-storey house, but it was quite large and had a lot of rooms." And from the early part of paragraph 25, I take it that you're describing the situation after you had left the Black Eagles. Answering the questions I just put to you, you gave me the impression that it was now and then you'd see an individual member of the Black Eagles; whereas, in paragraph 25 it very much looks as the Black Eagles being based in Glodjane in a structural way rather than just one or two of them going home for rest.

utterances.speaker: YLBER HASKAJ
utterances.text: I said then that they were based in Irzniq, but of course during combat activities they did not have time to stay there, because they were participating in the fighting. One or two members of this unit that were my co-villagers, they would return to the village to rest, as I said, or maybe they were wounded. So that's how I saw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for those answers. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I think there's just a typo in the transcript. Line 25 of the previous page, page 63. I think you said Irzniq, not Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, as a matter of fact he said "Gllogjan" and the witness said "Irzniq." MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, I see. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're now looking at what line? MR. DI FAZIO: 25. 25 of page 63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I misspoke, then -- of course, I was referring to paragraph 25, which doesn't speak about Glodjane. So I apologise for having misspoken there. Have the questions by the Bench raised any need for further questions by the parties? Then, Mr. Haskaj, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and answering all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Am I allowed to greet the commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, greeting commanders is not something -- you appeared here as a witness, and from your -- what you just said, I do understand that you would wish to do that, and I think that would be enough for one of the accused here to understand. Thank you very much. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then progress was made, I take it, that during the examination of the witness -- well, further progress was made. What would be the suggestion of the parties how to proceed to see whether we can ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry not to be able to respond decisively and conclusively. What I anticipate is that we might be able to put Mr. Sandhu in the witness box for a very short period of time just to deal with one or two matters to confirm his statement and deal with one matter of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that already seems to answer a couple of questions. I don't know whether the other Defence counsel are joining. Because -- first of all, the first question was whether Mr. Sandhu should be restored on the witness list. From your observation, I take it that there's no major objection against that. Or -- or would it be to find out whether there's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, because of the way in which this matter has arisen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- where we've been obviously taking instructions from clients on the changes to the last witness's 92 ter statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- whilst at the same time trying to resolve this matter, and so we're -- the emphasis is -- is on the preface to my last remarks, which is I'm not in a position to respond conclusively at this stage, but what we would anticipate may happen is that the witness could be recalled to give -- give evidence live. But may I -- I haven't consulted with my colleagues. I don't know what the attitude of the co-accused are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not talking about Mr. Sandhu.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. It's not recalled. That's a mistake. Re-introduced as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Re-introduced as a witness. Because let me just ... One second, please. You said earlier, "What I anticipate is that we might be able to put Mr. Sandhu in the witness box for a very short period of time."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to deal with one -- so you're considering whether you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a suggestion but something you'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, we'd like to have an opportunity to just consider it with co-accused counsel and with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how much time would you need to far?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In terms of resolving our position, ten minutes would be more than sufficient. I don't know whether there's any representative of the Prosecution immediately available who will deal with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who will deal with Mr. Sandhu? MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Re. Mr. Re will deal with Mr. Sandhu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that -- but not until after -- I'm not making any suggestion until after I've heard Mr. Guy-Smith, who is on his feet. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that's probably a -- a sensible suggestion, given the state of affairs. And I do have another very brief matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would, once again, request that any and all proofing notes that occurred after a five-hour meeting with the Prosecution be forwarded to us. We've received none. With regard to the last witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the record as well. Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honour, you will note that Mr. Harvey is not present in court, though he is available. And I can speak to him. For my own part, I would appreciate a slightly longer period than ten minutes in which to discuss the matter over the phone with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock. I suggest that we take our second break now; that we would resume at 20 minutes past 12.00; and that we would then have one hour and 25 minutes remaining. And if parties could agree or if the Chamber would determine so, that we would then use that time to hear the testimony of Mr. Sandhu, if he will be restored on the list and whether that would be 92 bis or 92 ter, I take it - but of course I'm not quite sure - that 92 ter might even go quicker than 92 bis, because we first would then need an officer being appointed by the Registrar to take a attestation and perhaps 92 ter would go by far quicker. Or is that wrongly understood, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I can agree with -- with the general observation it's going to be faster if it's 93 ter [sic]. But I don't want to pin my colleagues down not having discussed the matter in detail with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll hear then from you -- by the way, you are going so quickly you are even moving to 93 ter. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm still talking about 92 ter. MR. DI FAZIO: It's a linguistic tick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before we take the break if we could deal with one housekeeping matter. Some months ago we were dealing with the issue of height -- specifically with the issue of height of my client. We have received from the Detention Unit and it is now in e-court as 2D000767, a document that was created by the Detention Unit that indicates his height and weight and other physical characteristics. I've spoken with the Prosecution about this. I would seek an MFI number and seek its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D205.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then we'll have a look at the results. Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's just one final thing. Could I make a request to the Prosecution in relation to Mr. Sandhu, if there are any notes made, investigator's notes made in relation to the incident in which he describes and which is at issue, whether those could be disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you can't answer the question at this moment, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I will certainly convey the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that this will be part of the communications. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Just one more matter. I misled Defence counsel. It's in fact Mr. Dutertre who's dealing with this -- this matter and not Mr. Re, as I mentioned earlier. So any inquiries, if -- in the break, should they be made to the Prosecutors, Mr. Dutertre is the man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre is the man. That, I think, is a good line to start the break. We'll have a break until 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties inform the Chamber in relation to restoring Mr. Sandhu to the witness list whether there's any agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is agreement, and there's no objection to him being restored to the witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Dutertre, I was informed that the witness is waiting outside, which is not needed if there is a 92 bis statement. For 92 ter, however, he should enter the courtroom. Is that what you suggest? Yes, you're nodding "yes." Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Are there any issues about a 92 ter approach to this witness? That means that he does not -- I mean, until now we have just restored him on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we now know that Mr. Dutertre has -- I asked him -- is suggesting that we would have a 92 ter witness rather than a witness who viva voce is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Entirely acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, then the next issue is whether, in relation to the statement given by the witness, there's any dispute about -- I'm not suggesting that there should be, but just to take things step by step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And from your silence, I take it that there's no dispute about the admissibility of the statement under Rule 92 ter. Yes. One -- one second. Could you please sit down for a moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, let's take it step by step. First of all, the Chamber grants the application to restore Harjit Sandhu to the witness list. And that's, I think, the first decision we'll have to take. Now, Mr. Sandhu, you entered into the courtroom. Could you please stand. Mr. Sandhu, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Sandhu.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, a decision on admission of the 92 ter statement of Mr. Sandhu will be taken after you've asked the relevant questions and once the statement as such has been marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sandhu, I will first check your identity. You are called Harjit Sandhu. You were born on the 1st of January, 1956 at Amristar in India -- at Amristar in India, and you are -- Amristar -- and you are a team leader in the ICTY. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although on paper it's Amritsar instead of Amristar. I take it that Amritsar is better known to me as a place in India as Amristar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. I will pronounce it. It is Amritsar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sandhu, I will first ask for a document, 2148 of the 65 ter list. And perhaps the usher could bring a little file with the 92 ter and annexes document. If it could be brought here. 2143 of the 65 ter list. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have this on the screen as well in e-court. There it is. Madam Usher, if you would ....

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sandhu, did you sign this interview on the 5th of November, and is it truthful? Does it tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I signed it and these are my signatures and everything I said there is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The second question, Mr. Sandhu. On the matters which are -- which were discussed in this paper where asked from you today in this room, would you make the same answers as those which you made for your interview?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will make exactly the same answers if I am asked here in live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could this interview 92 ter be admitted, and as well as the two annexes with a reference of the last page with numbers of 65 ter list 988 and 989 of the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want them to have -- to have them under one exhibit number, so being attachments to the statement and be included in the same number assigned or separate?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Separate. Separate, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, the first annex, being the exhumation file in the case of Skender Kuqi, would receive what number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as P1218.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Then the -- second, the autopsy report on the body of Skender Kuqi. And, Mr. Dutertre, I have seen a provisional one which appears to be part of annex 1 and -- but I take it that you are referring to the autopsy report prepared by - let me just look at it again - by Dr. Morcillo. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. There's the anthropologist who has given his own findings before the report, and then there is the post-mortem report of the pathologist also, which comes after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I made a mistake. I said "autopsy report." There are two. But the first one actually is a report by a forensic anthropologist, Mr. Jose Pablo Baraybar, and that's part of the first annex. Is that correctly understood? And on the second annex is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- autopsy by Dr. Morcillo, a forensic medical doctor. This second, then, the forensic report would receive what number, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1219, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is one number, ERN. Only one number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the statement has not yet received a number. That's the 92 ter statement. Yes, Mr. Registrar, the 92 ter statement of Mr. Sandhu, which is the statement given on the 5th of November, 2007, would receive what number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any objection against admission of either the 92 ter statement or the two annexes to it? Then P1218, P1219, and P1220 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Dutertre, is there any need to -- for examination of the witness on your part?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few brief questions to ask from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sandhu, approximately what was the age of Genc Kuqi, the son of Skender Kuqi, on the day he brought you to the grave of his father to be exhumated, for the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Your Honours, he should be something like around 20. Maybe plus/minus could be, but around 20 I would put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was he hesitant to find the grave of his father, Skender Kuqi?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Your Honours, he was absolutely not hesitant. He was, rather, very helpful, cooperative, because he had already lodged a complaint with the UNMIK and when he came to know that we were going to look into that, he was excited. So it was not only us trying to locate him. He himself was keen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you can understand these questions in two different ways: Whether there was any hesitation at -- pointing at which was the grave of his father; or, as you answered it, whether he was hesitant to cooperate with ... Could you also focus on the second, whether he -- he was at any moment hesitant when he pointed at the grave of his father.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I respond like this that -- if I'd rather -- the way we proceeded chronologically, it will explain it clearly. And later on I can clarify if there is anything. When we picked him up and we arrived at the place, there were already his family members there. And immediately -- he said "stop." I was driving. He said, "Stop here. We have reached." And then straight away those -- his -- his mother and one or two uncles were around the grave, and he straight away told me that, "This is the grave of my father."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: This was indeed the meaning of my question. You said, at line 3, page 77, that "some members of his family were present." And in your interview, 92 ter paragraph 9, you say, "There were about eight to ten members of the family were present." How do you know that they were all members of the family of Genc Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: The minute I stopped the car, I asked him, "Who are these people." As a law enforcement officer, my first concern was is there any objection from the local villagers or something, is there a law and order problem. So the moment I saw them, I asked him, "Who are these people?" He said, "They are my family. My mother is there and some uncles from," if I remember correctly, from his mother's side there were those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he speak to them? Did he gather with them? Did Genc Kuqi talk to them and go towards them?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: After stopping, first he went to them. They were almost -- they were right on the road. And after stopping, he straight away went to that group and talked to them and then they all -- in fact, it was within 4 or 5 metres of the grave, they were all standing there. Am I clear on that point or do I elaborate it further?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: No, no, thank you very much. This is sufficient. You were present, Mr. Sandhu, during all the exhumation operations. Were other people than the OMPF representatives of the missing persons of the UNMIK, were other people, did they have access to the body?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Your Honours, when we reached there and he pointed out that this is the grave and then OMPF official Patrice Gagnon, he was with me, then he said these family members are allowed to attend but they have to stay a few metres away from that. So during the actual exhumation, it was only the OMPF people, myself, standing there as a -- as a guard or as a coordinator between the family, and -- and the family members were about 10 metres -- kept 10 metres away. And around the grave only the OMPF staff and their diggers and myself were there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: A follow-up question: When the OMPF left with the body, nobody else than the OMPF personnel had touched the body or manipulated the body? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: That's correct. Right from the moment we started the first digging, there was no one other than the OMPF people who had access. So right throughout till they -- they'd finished their job, till then no one else had access. Only when the remains were taken out, labeled on the bag, the wife of Skender Kuqi wanted to do a prayer and she was allowed just to come near and not -- not very close, and then she bent down and prayed. And after that the OMPF people left. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Last -- one but last point. I would like to have document 1218, last page, on the screens, please. And this should be 1219, unless I'm mistaken. We are seeing now -- so this is my mistake. I should like to see 1219, last page, please. That's it. Thank you. Mr. Sandhu, these photographs, do they actually show what you have seen on that particular day, on the 9th of March, 2004, when the exhumation took place, the body of Skender Kuqi was exhumated?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, these are exactly the pictures. And I was standing hardly one -- maximum 1 or 2 metres from the boundary of this picture. And these are the same pictures which were taken that day, and I very clearly remember this label, "SSA 01," and then they labeled it and one person went down -- the coffin was full of water even above that and it was taken out. And these is exactly the same pictures, I can recognise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions to ask, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson. Cross-examination by Mr. Emmerson

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sandhu, just one or more matters very briefly for the sake of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sandhu, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Just to repeat that, I've just got one or two matters for clarification to ask you about. In paragraph 9 of your statement, you record that though there were family members present, you did not specifically ask them their relationships with Skender Kuqi. Did you have conversations with any of the other family members that you recorded at the time?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Your Honours, I only spoke to Genc Kuqi, because we already knew -- the team knew Genc Kuqi so he was our only contact. And when Genc Kuqi told me they are his family members, I did not speak to any one of them, until in the end, when I just gave them my general condolences. And that was not addressed to any one, but to the entire family, I said, "I'm sorry for all this we have to do."

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. And all the information that you had and you were working on was information that you had obtained from Genc Kuqi alone.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes. You gave us an estimate of his age. I think we have a record from an interview that was given by him to the Office of the Prosecution in 2002 that puts his date of birth as the 2nd of October, 1982, which would, unless my calculations are incorrect, I -- I'm sure somebody will tell me that they are -- make him 15 at the date of the summer of 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we talking about the summer of 1998 or are we talking about before?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Unless my -- unless my calculations are incorrect, Genc Kuqi on that date of birth would have been 15 years old in the summer of 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Sandhu gave us an estimate of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 20 -- roughly 20 at the time of the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which was not in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, which was in 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the statement that he'd made in 2002?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: As the -- as the investigator on that team, we all discussed about the entire case of Skender Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes. Just one question, Mr. Sandhu. It follows from that, does it, that you were aware that he had not been present when his father was buried, because that's what he says in his witness statement. I'll just read you the sentence: "I was not permitted to attend the funeral because it was considered to be too dangerous to travel to that area." So we can take it that you were aware that he had not in fact attended the funeral.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: I don't exactly remember that, but my -- my task was clearly that I have to coordinate with him. And when he said that these are my relatives and they were all there, I didn't ask him whether he attended the original funeral, because I never asked him that question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: No, but -- but you can take it from me - and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong - that that's what he had told the Prosecution in his 2002 witness statement and presumably, as you've just told us, you would have been familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: I would say it this way: That I never personally interviewed or -- interviewed or took statement from him. The other team investigators did take. And the case as a whole, we did discuss several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. But you've told us he was the sole source of your information as to which was the right grave. How many graves were there in Dubovik cemetery?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: It was full of snow, and I won't be able to count, because snow was quite heavy. And only on this grave and there was one nearby visible. And we did not venture further into the graveyard to see. And this was -- this was one of the very few -- in the beginning itself, this grave was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: And they had already -- the family had already prepared it before we reached there. They were already standing around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. And --

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: So I take it that obviously his family members must have told him. His mother was there. His uncles were there. So if they were during the original burial -- I know Grbala [phoen] family were from my -- my knowledge of the case and as a team leader, I have -- I know almost every witness a little bit, as a summary about everything. I know Grbala family is from Dubovik. That is why the family -- that body was buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, I'm not asking you to -- to give broader information.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'm concentrating on the position as far as Genc Kuqi is concerned. And -- and finally this: You say in your statement you don't recall there being any marker on the grave as you saw it which identified it as being Skender Kuqi's grave.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Those just were the matters of clarification I wanted to seek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: No questions either, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it from any absence of questions there that although it's not fully documented that the body that was exhumed is the same body as is the subject of the autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm reluctant at this stage on behalf of myself or other counsel to make any formal concession which is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- currently in the agreed facts. We will obviously study the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we see quite some similarity in the -- in the forensic anthropologist's December 2004 description of the body compared to the autopsy report that was made in -- no, well, to be quite honest ... I'm looking at it. Mr. Dutertre, perhaps you could help us out. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The autopsy was signed April the 12th, 2004. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you inform us, because I'm -- I'm thinking in terms of who took the body, where, and it appears - but perhaps it's an attachment to your statement, Mr. Sandhu. Are you aware - because this is -- although it's an annex to your statement, the preliminary report on a case by Jose Pablo Baraybar, forensic anthropologist. Could you tell us exactly who gave to whom the body. It first went to the autopsy person and then he later then said -- how did it finally end up in the hands of the forensic anthropologist? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: Your Honour, OMPF personnel were there, they were the ones who were doing the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HARJIT SANDHU
utterances.text: I clearly remember Patrice Gagnon, he was the person who was speaking to me. He belonged to the same organisation as Jose Pablo Baraybar. He was -- we can say almost he was deputy to Jose Pablo Baraybar. So when he picked up the body, he was in charge of that. And it is the same organisation in the OMPF when he marked it as SSA 01, so after that that body is taken -- within the OMPF, who did it, who was assigned particular part, that, I think, only OMPF should be able to clarify that. But for me it was enough that OMPF had taken the body and this report was given to us by the OMPF.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we first see a autopsy report which is dated -- autopsy dated 12th of April. And then we see the forensic anthropologist giving a preliminary report on the findings of the post-mortem examination of a body identified as Skender Kuqi, yes, which is dated the -- December 2004. And I'm -- I'm asking myself, Mr. Dutertre, how to interpret everything, because there might be an issue, at least, that we cannot exclude for that in -- if we listen to the questions put to the witness by -- by Mr. Emmerson, that matters such as injuries or measurements, to the extent that they are the same in the two reports, that seems to be easily explained because the second report -- the December 2004 report says that it's based on the earlier autopsy report. Is that how we have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, this is a personal observation. But from the knowledge I have, the anthropologist is present during the autopsy and a difference in dates can be explained by the fact that the autopsy report was typed in April; where -- whereas -- that's just an observation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If people speak together, the interpreters are totally unable - unable to interpret, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, it was not without reason that the interpreters said two times "unable." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. I would object to Mr. Dutertre testifying about the manner in which examinations are performed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is no evidence of that at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he's not testifying. What he says is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: From the knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. From the -- the language is: "From the knowledge I have the anthropologist is present during the autopsy. And a difference in dates can be explained by the fact that the autopsy report was typed in April." And then afterwards -- and then he -- he puts in the language "that's just an observation." But the information given to the Chamber is factual in nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber understands this as not personal observation of Mr. Dutertre but what he -- what he thinks - not more than that - that has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which sometimes guides us on how to establish matters. Sometimes a starting point. If someone says, "Well, that happens quite a couple of times that my information is that," et cetera, et cetera, and then you can more focus better on to establish or avoid the issue. Mr. Dutertre, I -- I was just trying to -- to understand the -- the two reports in their context. Mr. Dutertre, you would certainly agree with me that the presence of the anthropologist during the autopsy does not appear from this evidence which -- this is evidence admitted. Now could we ask the witness: Do you have any further knowledge as to how the anthropologist who made the report, which is an annex to your statement, apart from, as he says in his report, the discussion and the conclusions based on the original autopsy report, do you know anything about whether he worked exclusively on the basis of the report, whether he has seen the body, whether he was present during the autopsy? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will -- I would try to explain it as clearly as I remember. I had another colleague investigator Howard Tucker, who was dealing with this issue. And in between I assisted him. That time I was not the investigations team leader. So I was one of the investigators. And when this report did not come for quite some time, then Howard started out telling, amongst the investigators, "We need to get in touch with that."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "this report." Are you talking about autopsy report or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both, Your Honour. Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So then I remember Howard talking to Jose Pablo Baraybar and trying to get -- so Jose Pablo, if I remember correctly, he did say, "Of course, Howard is the person who knows it directly." Mine is what I heard from him. And my desk was next to his desk. We were sitting that time together in the same room. So then he -- Jose Pablo told him that the report from -- the post-mortem, the first one, has come and I have to add my report on that and I have seen the body. It will be done. So this is what I heard. I -- I can't base it on any -- any documentary evidence. And later on this -- both the -- both the reports were put in evidence together by Howard. And then he circulated to the team that, okay, this is the autopsy report and he circulated this as a combined one. So Jose Pablo Baraybar's report, as well as the other one, released to us. But these are, of course, definitely two different reports. And to my understanding, Jose Pablo Baraybar was there present when this examination was done, not in the Dubovik village in the grave, but in the -- wherever this in the mortuary the examination was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's based on what you heard from your colleague at the time? Is that correctly understood? Because you said "to your understanding." And that understanding is based on -- on what you learned from Howard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour. That is what I heard from him. And in a general discussion, not addressed to me; like, just as -- in the room, general discussion, type of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need to put further questions to the witness? If not, then this concludes your evidence, Mr. Sandhu. Usually I thank witnesses for coming the long way to The Hague, but I think that would not be appropriate at this moment. Nevertheless, I would like to thank you for coming to court and to answer questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's on another matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on another matter. Well, we have some time left, so other matters are welcome at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's been suggested by the registrar that there may be some information contained in D205 that should be confidential, because it identifies certain matters with regard to the facility at UNDU. And I had been asked to put it under seal and I'm asking at this point that that document be put under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The whole of the document to be put under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, since there are no objections by the Prosecution, D205 should be under seal. Is there any other matter at this moment to be raised? Mr. Re, you are entering the courtroom at the moment when I asked the parties whether there's any other matter to be raised at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I'm here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm here. Witness scheduling. If I could raise those matters with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can we do that in open court or should we -- because there were -- perhaps there may be protective measures still to be granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's one -- one matter in relation to the Human Rights Watch witness, Mr. Abrahams --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. I'm aware of that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not a matter requiring closed -- protective measures. There's one -- there's two witnesses we're trying to get -- or who are obtaining travel documents who may require protective measures. We don't have an application yet from them. So if the names need to be mentioned, we would certainly do that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First let me -- because everything comes in so quickly. Mr. Abrahams you applied for admission under 92 bis or ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 92 -- 92 ter. Mr. Abrahams, the situation is we've been trying to get him -- we've been trying to get him to The Hague for some time. We were trying to get him in October, but he had to go to Gaza with Human Rights Watch and didn't return until the last week of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's, I think, in your --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. And then embarked upon a -- a business tour with the Human Rights Watch of the United States. We were trying -- we put in an application for videolink next Monday or, alternatively, for the Trial Chamber to sit the following Monday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- to hear his -- his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm, as a matter of fact - and my colleague Judges, as far as I can speak for them as well -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are approximately halfway reading his 65 ter statement. We still have to make up our mind on whether it is -- whether a videolink is appropriate and whether -- so we first read it and we -- we expect to give a decision first thing tomorrow morning if we have reached any conclusion. But, of course, not until we have heard from the Defence whether there are any -- whether any objections. What I intended to say more or less is that by tomorrow morning we would be -- we would have finished our reading. So therefore perhaps it will be a good idea to hear from the Defence to the extent that they're able, because I think the application has been filed yesterday only, to hear from the Defence whether there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry. There is an update, which I should inform the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and parties about first. That is simply this: Human Rights Watch yesterday -- there's a time difference, of course -- informed us that Mr. Abrahams would be in Los Angeles on Monday. The following Monday they said he would either be in San Francisco or New York but he would not be able to travel to The Hague until the Tuesday, the 20th but could testify by videolink from their office. And I think the tests are being done on the Monday, the 19th, or next Monday which is the 12th from Los Angeles. I'm sorry that -- that's--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's on the record. Of course, the 20th is -- is, as a matter of fact, reserved for, I think, 98 bis applications rather than to hear any further testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I understand. But that's the -- that's where we are with Human Rights Watch and in terms of getting the witnesses -- the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the technical aspect. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I can put our position simply at this stage, which is we do not accept that the requirements of Rule 81 bis are made out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you are not thinking in terms of 98 bis. 92 ter or videolink?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm concerned about videolink at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me -- I think you said 98 bis or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I meant to say 81 bis, which is what I think I said. So far as videolink is concerned, we say that the test isn't met. There are also substantial objections to the admissibility of the material and opinion evidence contained within Mr. Abraham's statements which will need to be the subject in due course of a motion to the Trial Chamber for their exclusion. Now, obviously all of us are working very busily at the moment on a number of fronts, and so in terms of setting a timetable for the filing of the motion, we would certainly ask for a little time. But there is -- there is, as I've indicated, quite a lot of material in that statement that we say shouldn't properly be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say the requirements for videolink are not met, whatever the decision of the Chamber in this respect would be, at least there are substantial objections against the content of what is presented until now. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. I think Mr. Guy-Smith adverted yesterday to a decision in the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that certainly would form part of the objection. There's also quite a lot of material when one reads the statement which is simply bold opinion evidence. And so we -- we would question, frankly, whether or not this material is likely to be of very substantial value to the Chamber at the present stage of the proceedings. But that's a matter which we can address in a motion if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's a completely accurate statement of the state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Yes, I adopt Mr. Emmerson's submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, we are ten lines behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I did not follow the French translation. I still admire those who are translating our words one by one. Then is there any other matter on behalf of the parties to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If we could possibly move into closed -- private session for a moment in relation to the other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That -- this -- the matter I raised and -- substantively is that of agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the things I wonder about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution is very, very anxious to have agreed facts finalised as soon as possible. We have sent proposals backwards and forwards, including a proposed joint motion, and it is at the point where unless we can get agreement we will ask for the Trial Chamber's intervention to hold a Rule 65 ter conference to, so to speak, crack heads together, because as far as we've -- we're concerned, we've taken it as far as we can with the proposals and the agreement we've given the Defence. We can't take the matters which are in writing, the subject of the draft motion which we forwarded again last week, we can't take it any -- any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's no -- no need to be cracking heads in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber refrains from cracking heads, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is also aware that one of the powers the Chamber does not have is to force parties into an agreement where the Chamber can encourage, can stimulate, but cannot force parties into an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The position is that -- that absolute minor matters aside, the only issue that remains in dispute as far as the Haradinaj team is concerned on the forensic agreed facts, is the outstanding DNA in respect of the most recent newly identified set of remains as regards which we have an outstanding inquiry with our own expert seeking confirmation of the validity of the material supplied by the Prosecution. Until we have that, we're not in a position to agree that particular fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But why not exclude that and put that as a separate issue when --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It can certainly be done. It can certainly be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's what we've been trying to do for -- for weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So where there's a 99 per cent agreement and a 1 per cent nonagreement, that the 1 per cent might be separated from the 99 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely and -- and I make it clear I'm speaking on behalf of the Haradinaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because Mr. Guy-Smith is on his feet as well and he'll explain his position, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps I am mistaken, but working towards a resolution I had understood that it was the preference of the Prosecution to have one document and one document alone so that we took care of this all at the same time. However, if that's not the case, then I don't think we have any difficulty whatsoever. And I don't take a position different from that just articulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So no heads being cracked. Mr. Troop, is -- you're also in favour of the separation of the 1 per cent from the 99 per cent?

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: I have very little to add, but I'm sure resolution can be reached quite easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The motion is ready to be filed. We have it in draft form with the annex. The names of all the lead counsel on it. It's ready to sign. It's ready to be filed. If -- if that's where we are, we can -- I can see nodding from across the Defence bench. We can sign it and file it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is looking forward to it. Let's leave it at that. Then the -- any other matter to be raised by the parties? Then the Chamber would like to have all submissions by the Defence on the admission of the annexes on the (redacted) ter statement annexes by the housekeeping session of -- on the 8th of November so that we have all -- so that would be at the latest at that moment. We have already a motion from the Haradinaj Defence to exclude portions of the statements and certain of the attachments. So whatever else is there to be said about these matters, we'd like to know that at the latest the 8th of November. Let me just see whether I have any other matter. Yes. There is a Rule 92 quater motion in which I think there was one -- there was a 92 bis application was withdrawn and there was an application for admission under 92 quater. I don't know whether I could mention names at this moment, but the Chamber would very much like the Defence to respond to it by the 6th of November. Is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It might be difficult, because we were obtaining --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, today is -- today is the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're obtaining medical information, and the witness is, we're told, is now in Kosovo. So we're trying to find the witness's medical practitioner there to provide us with the information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you would then make that part of your communications this afternoon as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we hear -- of course, the 6th is already today. So at earliest --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For -- for the Chamber's information, just to make sure that we're clear about things, the Balaj Defence filed on the 27th of October its objections to the (redacted) statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have -- I have that. Therefore, I said if there's anything else to be said about it, then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was an issue on the 2nd of November about lists that were provisional and final versions still to be expected. In this respect, I -- by the way, Mr. Registrar is preparing a redaction. I'll -- I'll further explain that to the parties out of court. There's an issue still pending on this which ... Then -- yes. As far as MFI D41 is concerned, that's a lengthy video where the Chamber invited you -- there was no objection against admission, but looking at this video, it takes hours and hours, and I think it should be reduced to the -- to the swearing-in ceremony only. When could we expect that, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Then there is another matter. As far as P367 is concerned, there were some questions about whether it was admitted or not, but the parties were then invited to make any submissions -- further submissions on P367. The Chamber would very much like to determine the matter on the next housekeeping session. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I can indicate what the issue was, I think I may have touched on it once before. There's an expression of opinion in the document which is outside of the witness's area of expertise, and it's in respect of that that we take objection. I can discuss it with Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, would that be a possibility for you to discuss it with Mr. Emmerson and then to see whether it's a vital portion, whether the Chamber would have to decide over your --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can discuss it now, Mr. President. The only thing is that when I permitted 92 ter, no objection had been made at the time, so I think the objection of Mr. Emmerson comes a bit later -- a bit late, but I can ask him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know if Mr. Dutertre and the Trial Chamber recalls, but the practice that we evolved of raising objections and having them determined by agreement and by the Bench if there was no agreement evolved after Mr. Seif [phoen] has testified and I raise the issue about the inclusion of that passage in his statement at the time that he testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would prefer if the parties would agree on whether or not to leave that specific portion in. I have no clear memory at this moment about the matter. Then -- yes, then there's another matter still pending. Mr. Re, D64, D65, and D115, I think the -- your position was that the Prosecution had no objections to these exhibits being admitted but that you'd like to make submissions as to the weight that will be given to these. Now, first of all, I would like to enquire with you, Mr. Registrar. Do we know exactly at this moment how in your system D64, D65, and D115 are qualified, as still marked for identification or already admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, D64, D65, and D115 are all marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then since there are no objections, as I understand, they are admitted into evidence. At the same time, Mr. Re, if you'd like to make any submissions as to the weight, then you are, to a certain extent, free do so. That means that we do not enter into a complete debate on the weight to be given to it, but if you'd like to make some brief observations about it, the Chamber would not disallow you to do so. And not necessarily at this moment but --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, no, no, I wasn't going to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's just been drawn to my attention that D115 is -- is it an ECMM report? Was that a Rule 70 document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that just be checked before it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you make your submissions on the weight to be given to it, then you will certainly refer to what the content of it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, no, all I'm asking at the moment is, I just need to check whether it's a document provided -- that should be exhibited under seal, D115. That was all, if it could just remain under seal at the moment until I make any inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then for the time being, could you inform the Chamber about that at the earliest occasion. Yes, as far as Witness 69 is concerned, there was an issue about P1181. And I do understand that still further submissions by the Defence are expected. Then if there's nothing else to be raised at this moment, we will adjourn until tomorrow, the 7th of November, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
